profiles.label: Worksheet / Practice
profiles.summary: Create a focused student practice resource with a clear progression, usable workspace, and an optional answer key.
rules: Every problem must align to the submitted learning target(s).
Use meaningful progression rather than filler or repeated busywork.
Provide enough workspace for the actual response demands.
When an answer key is requested, it must match the final student version exactly.

profiles.label: Differentiated Worksheet
profiles.summary: Create aligned versions that preserve the same core learning target while varying support, complexity, or access.
rules: All versions must stay anchored to the same essential learning target(s).
Do not turn the supported version into trivial work or the advanced version into unrelated content.
Use neutral student-facing labels such as Version A, Version B, and Version C unless the teacher explicitly requests other labels.
Teacher notes must explain the instructional differences among versions.

profiles.label: Extension Activity
profiles.summary: Create meaningful transfer, application, synthesis, or design work for students ready to go beyond routine practice.

controls.label: Build from students' current/previous work when source material supports it

rules: Extension means transfer, synthesis, design, comparison, investigation, or deeper reasoning—not simply more of the same questions.
Use prior student work only when it is actually included or clearly described.
Keep the activity realistically completable within the stated time or flag the mismatch in the teacher guide.

profiles.label: Formative Assessment
profiles.summary: Create a diagnostic check that reveals what students understand, where reasoning breaks down, and what to teach next.
rules: The assessment should diagnose thinking, not merely produce a score.
Use plausible distractors or prompts tied to likely reasoning errors when appropriate.
When misconception notes are requested, connect them to specific items and actionable next steps.

profiles.label: Rubric
profiles.summary: Create an observable, growth-oriented scoring tool aligned to the actual task and evidence students are expected to produce.
rules: Criteria and descriptors must be specific and observable, not vague adjectives alone.
Reward reasoning, evidence, iteration, revision, or process when those matter to the submitted task.
Do not invent criteria unrelated to the learning target or uploaded assignment.

profiles.label: Lesson Plan / Lesson Outline
profiles.summary: Create a realistic lesson sequence with clear targets, timing, checks for understanding, and ready-to-use teacher moves.
rules: Total planned time must be realistic for the stated class period.
Include at least one meaningful check for understanding unless the teacher explicitly disables it in notes.
Prefer active student thinking over lecture-heavy filler.

profiles.label: Presentation / Lesson Slides
profiles.summary: Create a classroom-ready slide deck with readable design, instructional visuals, and optional speaker notes and formative checks.

controls.label: Also include a concise student handout / notes page

rules: Use a readable 16:9 presentation with strong contrast and restrained district navy/blue styling.
Do not shrink body text to fit excessive content; split ideas across slides instead.
Use real diagrams, graphs, images, or tables when they materially support understanding.
Speaker notes, when requested, must match the final slide sequence and not describe slides that do not exist.

profiles.label: Stations
profiles.summary: Create a set of student stations with clear directions, realistic materials, print-ready pages, and an optional answer key.

controls.label: Keep each station to one student page when practical

rules: Each station needs a distinct purpose and should contribute to the same target set rather than repeat identical questions.
Materials must match the teacher selection and be clearly listed.
If one-page-per-station is selected, verify the actual PDF pages rather than assuming CSS fit.

profiles.label: Curriculum / Unit Outline
profiles.summary: Create a coherent multi-day or multi-week unit map with pacing, learning progression, assessment checkpoints, and differentiation opportunities.

controls.label: Include a summative assessment / performance task
Include hands-on / applied experiences when appropriate

rules: Build a coherent learning progression rather than a list of disconnected daily activities.
Keep pacing realistic for the stated calendar.
Connect assessments to the learning targets and identify where evidence is gathered.

profiles.label: Blooket Review
profiles.summary: Create a Blooket-ready CSV review set with strict import formatting and a separate teacher answer reference.

controls.label: Include calculation questions when appropriate to the subject

rules: The CSV itself must contain only import data—no markdown, explanations, or commentary.
Use the exact Blooket column order defined in the Resource Builder contract.
Correct Answer(s) must use numeric answer positions only.
Use plain text in the CSV; move rich math explanations to the teacher answer reference.

profiles.label: Other / Custom Resource
profiles.summary: Create a teacher-defined classroom resource while still inheriting the district build, rendering, styling, conflict, and QA standards.

controls.label: Include a brief teacher guide when useful

rules: Use the teacher's description and constraints to define the resource without silently inventing a different artifact type.
If best-fit format is selected, choose a practical classroom format and record the choice in QA.
Apply all shared district math, graph, visual, CSS, PDF, link, and conflict rules that are relevant to the chosen format.
